# Clanky iOS - Full Docs

> Clanky iOS is the native SwiftUI client for attaching to the Eve relay, inspecting herdr state, and steering Clanky work from a phone without inventing a second API.

Generated from the live docs site. Each section below is one page; see the heading and source path for context.

---

# Overview

Source: `README.md` - https://volpestyle.github.io/docs/clanky-ios/?doc=overview

# Clanky iOS

Native SwiftUI window for checking and steering Clanky from an iPhone. The app
talks to the Eve relay that Clanky's headless command host starts locally,
mirrors the live herdr workspace/tab/pane hierarchy, and sends operator input
back through the same relay contract used by the desktop tools.

## What You Can Do

- connect to an Eve relay over local network or Tailscale
- store the relay URL in app preferences and the relay bearer token in Keychain
- generate and store an ed25519 SSH lifecycle key in Keychain
- run `scripts/clanky-up.ts` over SSH in `up`, `status`, and `down` modes
- inspect herdr workspaces, tabs, panes, agents, and full retained terminal history
- choose native terminal attach or compatibility mirror mode per app install
- send text and special keys to a pane through `run` and `keys` relay ops
- launch and close herdr panes through the Clanky relay
- start or continue a chat-with-Clanky Eve session
- run Clanky slash commands through native iOS menus where the command makes sense on mobile

## Native UI Direction

Clanky iOS uses native SwiftUI app chrome around terminal content. Lists,
forms, toolbars, sheets, multiwindow, Dynamic Type, and system appearance follow
iPhone and iPad conventions; the terminal surface itself remains black and
monospaced so ANSI output stays faithful. The bundled mono face is JetBrains
Mono, matching the local Ghostty `font-family` setting. iPad layouts should use
split views, toolbar commands, wider pane tiles, and readable-width content
instead of stretching the iPhone bottom-bar flow.

Modal sheets use Liquid Glass presentation chrome on iOS 26+, with opaque
true-black fallbacks when Reduce Transparency is enabled. Screen-level content
surfaces remain flat so terminal output and dense workspace lists stay legible.

Terminal panes have two Settings-selectable stream modes. **Native** is the
default: it attaches to Herdr's durable terminal id when one is available and
resizes that server-owned terminal to the iOS grid. **Mirror** keeps the
compatibility path: the relay asks for Herdr's full retained scrollback when that
build supports it, otherwise it falls back to capped `recent_unwrapped` output
instead of surfacing a raw schema error. Terminal output uses the Ghostty VT
renderer for ANSI color fidelity, with the local retained grid capped at 32,000
rows for very large buffers. The terminal scroll range is virtualized: UIKit owns
the full scrollable height while the drawn terminal surface stays viewport-sized
and paints only visible rows. Terminal panes support pinch-to-zoom text sizing
that persists as the default across Agent tabs, with a typed Settings percentage,
matching toolbar controls, and a transient percentage HUD while zooming.

## Contract Boundary

This repository is the SwiftUI client only. The canonical API is the current
Clanky implementation in `../clanky`, especially:

- `SPEC.md` for the iOS window behavior
- `scripts/clanky-up.ts` for lifecycle bootstrap output
- `agent/channels/relay.ts` for relay operations and payloads
- `agent/lib/frontdoor-auth.ts` for bearer-token auth
- Eve session routes for chat-with-Clanky conversation state

When the app needs new behavior, update or document the Clanky contract first,
then wire the iOS integration against that contract.

## Mental Model

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  phone["Clanky iOS"]
  network["LAN / Tailscale"]
  sshd["sshd"]
  lifecycle["scripts/clanky-up.ts"]
  commandHost["Clanky command host"]
  eve["Eve front door"]
  relay["/relay/ws"]
  herdr["herdr workspace"]
  session["/eve/v1/session"]

  phone --> network
  network --> sshd
  network --> eve
  sshd --> lifecycle
  lifecycle --> herdr
  lifecycle --> commandHost
  commandHost --> eve
  eve --> relay
  eve --> session
  relay --> herdr
```

HTTP URLs are accepted for local/private LAN and Tailscale modes. Custom public
endpoints should use HTTPS.

## Connect

On first launch, copy the app's SSH public key from the connection screen and
add it to the Mac user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. Then enter the Mac SSH host,
user, port, Clanky repo path, relay URL, and relay token.

The app runs this lifecycle command over SSH before attaching to the relay. It
starts the headless Clanky command host, which owns the Eve server and executes
slash-command menu flows for the native iOS UI. A visible desktop face can be
open too, but iOS no longer depends on one:

```bash
cd <repoPath> && CLANKY_RELAY_TOKEN=<token> node scripts/clanky-up.ts --json
```

The `status` and `down` lifecycle modes are available from the connected room
actions sheet.

The app also accepts deep links of the form:

```text
clanky://connect?relayUrl=http://127.0.0.1:2000&token=...
```

For local simulator development, leaving SSH host empty still lets the app
attach to an already-running relay.

## Run

```bash
brew install xcodegen      # if not already installed
xcodegen generate
open ClankyIOS.xcodeproj
```

Command line:

```bash
xcodebuild -project ClankyIOS.xcodeproj \
  -scheme ClankyIOS \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' \
  build
```

Simulator terminal smoke test:

```bash
# Seeded terminal route, useful without a relay.
scripts/ios-simulator-terminal-smoke.sh

# Live relay route: connects to ../clanky, opens the first Herdr agent pane,
# captures a screenshot/log, and fails on known SwiftUI terminal freeze faults.
MODE=live DEVICE_NAME="iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)" scripts/ios-simulator-terminal-smoke.sh
MODE=live DEVICE_NAME="iPhone 17 Pro" scripts/ios-simulator-terminal-smoke.sh
```

The hosted docs UI renders this README as the source of truth.

```bash
pnpm docs:dev
pnpm docs:build
```


The seeded `AppStore.demo()` workspace uses Clanky/herdr sample data so the
window hierarchy can be inspected before connecting to a live relay.
